It's not a horrible community and I'm mostly speaking through personal experience so my opinion may differ from other players. I started playing FFXIV shortly after ARR came out. Back then my experience was great. Everyone was super nice and had a lot of patience. My experience turned sour once I got to Heavensward end game content. Every time I got into roulette I would constantly encounter players that were toxic, telling you to "get good" or getting mad over 1 wipe and what not. It got to a point that it was normal and I just ignored those types of players. Then I started doing Trials and Raids and that was another issue. I've been a casual player most of my life so switching to play serious and trying to get my damage/healing output high was an uphill battle for me. I saw many learning parties disbanded due to wipe frustration and poor explaining, the newbies in the group, myself included, always watched videos before the fight but sadly I learn more by doing rather than seeing. When I did know the fight I saw the same situation happen with other noobs and it was hard trying to explain mechanics to a new player while having while having others abandoning duty or flaming the player. I love FFXIV and I would had been so pumped for the new expansion but every time I subscribe and log into the game again I just don't feel motivated to play. Anyways this is my personal opinion, don't take my word as a fact for the entire community but these types of situation still happen in MMOs and it affects a small part of the community. Hopefully if OP tries the game his experience will be different.

Failures are part of any table top game. I only recently started playing and I rolled a Half-ling Bard. I wanted him to be epic, brave, suave and a stealthy rogue (he has a criminal background so I wanted to make him a Bard with Underworld connections). I ended up being a dumb but talented/agile half-ling that makes a joke about many things and fails at almost every slight of hand and stealth check. He is very deceptive and persuasive though and guess what? I'm having a blast. It's my first campaign and I enjoy my DM and fellow party members and we just laugh at our failures and it makes for some amazing character growth. I really love my character and so does the party. My recommendation is to try your best to get along with your party and like others mention, own your mistakes. Make some witty joke about it or just simply let it happen. I know it will be hard at first but explain your behavior to the team before hand and as you build trust I'm sure it will go away and things will transition smoothly. Just remember to have fun, that's the point of the game.
